definitions.gloss: tenure; being in office; holding a position
definitions.explanation: The period during which someone holds an official position or office. Used for political leaders, executives, and other officials.

examples.japanese: {在任|ざいにん}{中|ちゅう}に{多|おお}くの{改革|かいかく}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: Many reforms were carried out during their tenure.

examples.japanese: {在任|ざいにん}{期間|きかん}は4{年|ねん}だった。
examples.english: The term of office was four years.

examples.japanese: {歴代|れきだい}{首相|しゅしょう}の{中|なか}で{最|もっと}も{長|なが}く{在任|ざいにん}したのは{安倍|あべ}{晋三|しんぞう}だ。
examples.english: Among all prime ministers, Abe Shinzo served the longest tenure.

notes: Composed of {在|ざい} (exist, be present) + {任|にん} (duty, appointment). A formal term used in political and business reporting. Common collocations: {在任|ざいにん}{中|ちゅう} (during one's tenure), {在任|ざいにん}{期間|きかん} (period of office/tenure), {在任|ざいにん}{日数|にっすう} (number of days in office). Not to be confused with the homophone {罪人|ざいにん} (criminal, sinner), which has a completely different meaning and kanji. Similar terms: {在職|ざいしょく} (being employed/in a position — broader, includes non-official jobs), {任期|にんき} (term of office — the defined period rather than the act of holding office).
